description: The bar chart, titled “Targets,” illustrates the annual number of datasets categorized by whether they are “Untargeted” (blue) or “Targeted” (orange) from 2012 to 2022, as part of the systematic review “The Unseen Targets of Hate.” The horizontal axis represents the year, ranging from 2012 to 2022, while the vertical axis indicates the “Number of datasets,” scaled from 0 to 160 in increments of 20. Each year is represented by a stacked bar, with the blue segment at the bottom denoting “Untargeted” datasets and the orange segment on top representing “Targeted” datasets. In 2012 and 2013, only one or two datasets were recorded, all untargeted. From 2014 to 2016, datasets remain minimal, with a slight increase in 2016 (approximately 10 total, mostly targeted). A clear upward trend begins in 2017, with 28 total datasets (12 untargeted, 16 targeted), rising to 48 in 2018 (20 untargeted, 28 targeted), 65 in 2019 (12 untargeted, 53 targeted), 130 in 2020 (48 untargeted, 82 targeted), and peaking in 2021 with 158 total datasets (66 untargeted, 92 targeted). In 2022, the total drops to approximately 38 datasets (10 untargeted, 28 targeted). The chart visually emphasizes the growing prevalence of targeted hate datasets over time, particularly from 2017 onward, with 2021 showing the highest volume of both targeted and untargeted datasets.
